b64url.description: Strict canonical b64url decoding: RFC 4648 URL alphabet, no "=", reject any other char, length mod 4 = 1 and nonzero spare bits. ok true gives hex = the decoded bytes (hex here only, to avoid testing the codec with itself).

content_cap.description: Size cap: 2048 UTF-8 bytes of the raw url / text / tel string. ok = utf8_bytes <= 2048. truncated = the "send the first 2048 bytes" text cut on a UTF-8 code point boundary (equal to input when ok).

description: PushArmor golden cross-platform vectors v1 (normative; catalog r10). Binary values are strict b64url (RFC 4648 URL alphabet, no padding) unless a field says otherwise: b64url.cases[].hex and rfc9180 use hex. Ids are 40-char b64url; raw id bytes are their decoded 30 bytes. Times are unix seconds. Peers are named N, X, O, Z, S (see keys). Randomized primitives (ECDSA, HPKE seal) are checked in the verify/open direction; generator signatures use RFC 6979 and HPKE ephemeral keys use DeriveKeyPair(ikmE) only to make this file reproducible.

email_hash.description: Email normalization and email_hash (Worker). Trim ASCII whitespace (TAB LF VT FF CR SPACE) only, then any byte outside ASCII -> 400 "bad email" (normalized null; NBSP is not trimmed and so rejects), then ASCII lowercase A-Z -> a-z. email_hash = sha256("PA-ACCT1\n" || normalized), account = HMAC-SHA256(keys.id_secret, email_hash)[0..9]. Assert normalized, email_hash and account byte for byte.

id_order.description: Lower id for the crossing tie-break (I232): unsigned lexicographic compare of the decoded 30 raw id bytes, each byte 0..255. lower names the lower side ("a" or "b"). Every leg asserts every case.

inflate.description: deflate-raw (RFC 1951) inflate of the given bytes with a 16384-byte output cap. ok false = reject (over cap or invalid/truncated stream). Assert ok, inflated_len and inflated_sha256 (b64url); inflated is given when <= 256 bytes.

keys.description: Fixed test keys and ids. Private keys are raw 32-byte P-256 scalars, public keys 65-byte SEC1 points. id_secret is the test ID_SECRET. Assert byte for byte: sign_pub/enc_pub from the private scalars, account = HMAC-SHA256(id_secret, email_hash(email))[0..9], keyhash = sha256("PA-ID1\n" || sign_pub || enc_pub)[0..12], id = account || keyhash || HMAC-SHA256(id_secret, account || keyhash)[0..9]. N, X, O share account A; Z is on account B; S has sign_pub equal to enc_pub (negative cases only). Other sections refer to these peers by name.

messages.description: One full inner message per type, X -> N. JSON {"n": counter, type: value} -> deflate-raw (any valid stream is fine for senders; receivers inflate the given bytes) -> body = from id(30) || pairing id(8) || keys flag(1; 1 on approve, 0 on every other type) [|| sign_pub || enc_pub, approve only] || u16 BE deflated length || deflated -> zero pad so the wire length is the next of 512/1024/2048/3800 chars -> sig = ECDSA over "PA-MSG1\n" + recipient 40-char id + "\n" + padded body (signed_bytes) -> plaintext = sig || padded body -> HPKE (info "PA-MSG1", aad = recipient id) -> message = b64url(enc || ct). Receiver state: pin (the pinned keys, pairing id and ruling approved | unruled | denied of the sender), window (h and the seen n values), history (n values with a History row). Assert: open message with the receiver enc_priv and compare plaintext; verify sig before inflate; inflate deflated and compare json; run the full receive pipeline and compare expect (outcome, type, n, value; approve/rename value = verified name and n; the name entry n must equal the message n; the name entry is checked before the replay window).

must_fail.description: Inputs every client must reject, with the expected outcome: "invalid" (a replay: a seen n of url/text/tel with no History row, or n <= h - 100; notice and History event "Invalid message received") or "unreadable" (every other case: drop under the Notice rule, the generic "could not read"; for request and peer_entry kinds it means reject/drop with no Invalid notice). kind message: receiver state as in messages (pin null = sender not pinned); kind pair: open with the receiver key, kind must equal expected_kind, for open sha256("PA-SAS1C\n" || keys || r_N) must equal stored_c_N; kind name_entry: as name_entries with pin; kind request: verify PA-Sig over the fields (the Worker returns 401); kind peer_entry: a GET /peers entry checked against the receiver account (prefix, keyhash, valid 65-byte points, sign_pub != enc_pub). Every leg asserts every case and its outcome. Counter key is "n".

my_push_sha256.description:
my_push_sha256 = b64url(first 16 bytes of sha256(UTF-8 of: fcm, apns, apns-sandbox: type + "
" + token; webpush, unifiedpush: type + "
" + endpoint + "
" + p256dh + "
" + auth)). Field strings are used as given. Assert my_push_sha256.

name_entries.description:
Name entries. s = owner signature over "PA-NAME1
" + owner id + "
" + recipient id + "
" + pairing id (11 chars) + "
" + n + "
" + name (the b64url string). ciphertext = b64url(enc || ct), HPKE to the recipient enc_pub, info "PA-NAME1", aad = recipient 40-char id, at most 1024 chars. Assert signed_string from the fields; open ciphertext with the recipient enc_priv and compare entry_json; verify s with the owner sign_pub; name 1..32 printable ASCII.

oauth_nonce.description: OAuth nonce: k = b64url(sha256(sign_pub)), nonce = b64url(sha256("PA-NONCE1\n" + purpose + "\n" + k)) (k as its b64url string). Assert k and nonce.

padded_messages.description: One text message per padding bucket (512, 1024, 2048, 3800 wire chars), X -> N; the 3800 case carries 2048 bytes of content (the max-size padded message). Same format and assertions as messages; also assert message length == bucket.

padding.description: Padding math. plaintext_len = HPKE plaintext length before padding (sig 64 + body). unpadded_chars = ceil((plaintext_len + 81) * 4 / 3) (enc 65 + tag 16, b64url without "="). bucket = smallest of 512/1024/2048/3800 >= unpadded_chars, null = sender refuses (> 3800). padded_plaintext_len = bucket * 3 / 4 - 81.

pair_decide.description: PURE pairing decision on X for a commit push (Pairing flow step 3, rules a-e, first match wins; I239). Input fields: own_id, from_id; commit_c_N; entry (null or the open entry for from_id: role N|X, state N: committed|shown, X: replied|prompted|shown, c_N and reply_authorized for X role); pinned; approved (implies pinned); approve_verified (from_id's approve verified here); approves_me (last GET /peers, null if none) and get_after_verify (that GET was fetched after the approve verified); listed (yes | after_fetch | no: in the last GET /peers, after one fetch, still absent); open_entries (all roles); cap (unix s of counted automatic replies); now (unix s). Output: action reply|notice|abort|prompt|drop; notice commit ("A new peer wants to pair. Open PushArmor.") | half_state ("$X wants to pair again. Tap Cancel pairing on its row, then pair.", tag pk) | crossing ("Pairing with $X in progress. Open PushArmor.", platforms that notify every push only) | could_not_read (generic, platforms that notify every push only) | represent (re-present the current notice, same tag/id); entry created_replied | created_prompted | n_wiped_x_replied | aborted | unchanged | none; cap_counted (the reply counts in the cap). A cap timestamp t counts while now - t < 86400. Lower id = unsigned byte compare (see id_order). Every leg (android, ios, webext) asserts all four output fields.

pair_hint.description: N-side hint on a row in state committed (Pairing flow step 8). input: approves_me of X in the last GET /peers (null if none), committed_s (seconds in state committed). output: still_holds ("$X still holds an earlier pairing. On $X, tap Cancel pairing, then tap Send again.") | no_reply_yet ("No reply yet. Open PushArmor on $X, or tap Send again.", from 3 days) | null.

pair_timeout.description: Pairing timeout at 14 days (Pairing flow step 8). input: approve_verified (the other side's approve verified), approved (this device approved; with approve_verified false the row is "Waiting for $X"), resend (result of the re-send of POST /v1/approve/$X: null not run yet | offline | paused | 429 | 5xx | 200_c_verified | 200_other). output: keep_pin | drop_pin (drop r, c_N and the pin, show "Pairing timed out. Tap Pair to start again.", then the allow reconcile) | resend (run the re-send first) | keep_waiting (row stays Waiting with Cancel pairing; retry at next app open, Refresh or unpause) | complete (the verified c completes the pairing).

pairing.description:
One pairing of N (new peer) with X (existing peer). c_N = sha256("PA-SAS1C
" || sign_pub_N || enc_pub_N || r_N); fingerprint_hash = sha256("PA-SAS1
" || sign_pub_N || enc_pub_N || sign_pub_X || enc_pub_X || r_N || r_X); fingerprint = first 20 bits MSB first as 4 Crockford chars of "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ"; pairing_id = sha256("PA-PAIRID1
" || r_N || r_X)[0..8] (11-char b64url); pk = b64url(sha256("PA-PAIRKEY1
" || N id || X id)[0..16]) over the raw 30-byte ids, N first. pair_messages: plaintext = kind(1: commit, 2: reply, 3: open) || from id(30) || body(162), 193 bytes; HPKE info "PA-PAIR1", aad = recipient 40-char id; message = b64url(enc || ct), 366 chars. Assert c_N, fingerprint_hash, fingerprint, pairing_id, pk byte for byte; open each message with the recipient enc_priv and compare the plaintext; for the open, check sha256("PA-SAS1C
" || keys || r_N) equals c_N. fingerprint_cases check the 20-bit Crockford mapping (every symbol once). The hpke block (DeriveKeyPair(ikmE) ephemeral) is optional to assert.

phone.description: Phone number detection: trim ASCII whitespace (TAB LF FF CR SPACE) and NBSP, strip a leading "tel:", then phone iff ^\+?(?:[ ().-]*[0-9]){7,15}[ ().-]*$ (ASCII digits) and not IPv4 shape ^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$ and not date shape ^([0-9]{4}([-. ])[0-9]{2}\2[0-9]{2}|[0-9]{2}([-. ])[0-9]{2}\3[0-9]{4})$. Assert phone.

replay_window.description: Replay window per sender: h = highest accepted n, seen = the n values whose bit is set (bit k = n = h - k, k 0..99), listed high to low. Accept iff n > h - 100 and n not seen; on accept with n > h shift (h = n, drop bits past 99), else set the bit. A rejected n: n <= h - 100 -> invalid; seen n of a control type (approve rename remove delete pause unpause deny) -> noop; seen n of url/text/tel with a History row -> represent; else invalid. Assert outcome and state_after (equal to state when not accepted).

request_sig.description:
PA-Sig: ECDSA P-256 SHA-256 raw r||s over "PA-REQ1
" + METHOD + "
" + path + "
" + PA-Time + "
" + raw body bytes; path includes /v1, no query string; empty body = zero bytes; PA-Time 13 decimal digits. Assert signed_bytes byte for byte from the fields, and that sig verifies with sign_pub (ECDSA is randomized: verify only).

rfc8291.description: RFC 8291 section 5 example with the Appendix A intermediate values (base64url as in the RFC). Assert the derivation from as_private, ua_public, auth_secret and salt (record size 4096) gives every intermediate and body byte for byte, and that decrypting body with ua_private gives plaintext.

rfc9180.description: RFC 9180 base mode, DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM (kem 16, kdf 1, aead 2): the entry from the test vector file RFC 9180 cites ([TestVectors], cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-hpke commit 5f503c56). Values in hex as in the source. Assert DeriveKeyPair(ikmE/ikmR) -> skEm/skRm, the key schedule (shared_secret, key_schedule_context, secret, key, base_nonce, exporter_secret), seal of pt with aad == ct at sequence 0, and open.

url_parse.description: Received url: a strict URL parse, scheme http or https (any case), non-empty host, no userinfo; url false = shown as a plain text notification. href = WHATWG URL().href shown in notification, History and Open; host = the parsed hostname shown to the user (IDN as punycode). auto_open (extensions only): https, DNS hostname, no IP literal, no explicit port, at least two labels after stripping one trailing dot, not "localhost", last label not "localhost" or "local".
